dedupe_keys.name: 6g resilience white paper resilience as a primary design goal with the 3r framework arxiv 2025

description: This white paper argues that 6G must be designed to withstand, adapt to and evolve amid prolonged, complex disruptions, making resilience a primary design goal alongside sustainability and efficiency, across technology, architecture and economics. It analyses dependencies between mobile networks and other critical systems such as energy, transport and emergency services, illustrates how cascading failures spread, and formalises resilience with the 3R framework. Enablers include programmability for islanded operation, fallback modes and multi-layer diversity of radio, compute, energy and timing, AI-native control loops with verifiable behaviour, zero-trust security rooted in hardware and supply-chain integrity, and prioritisation of critical and time-sensitive traffic. It also identifies nine business-model groups and outlines governance and standardisation. Producer: 39 authors led by Hirley Alves, submitted 10 September 2025. Coverage: global, conceptual. Access: free arXiv preprint; only the abstract page was read. Licence and cost: free to read; licence arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (the paper; no open reuse licence). Caveats: a position paper without datasets or code, and the 3R definitions were not read. Simulation uses: the dependency analysis and cascading-failure illustrations give structure for coupled resilience models of mobile networks and energy or transport systems. Related record: the ITU Connect2Recover resilience study (case_study-itu-connect2recover-national-ict-infrastructure-resilience-asia-pacifi).
